findings.issue: The dependency graph contains a cycle: T1 → T2 → T3 → T1.
findings.evidence: T1 after=[T3]; T2 after=[T1]; T3 after=[T2].
findings.failure_scenario: None of T1, T2 or T3 can start while respecting its prerequisites, blocking implementation and final verification.
findings.fix: Remove T3 from T1's prerequisites. Retain T1 → T2 → T3; the derived snapshot is explicitly not a deployment prerequisite.

findings.issue: T2 and T4 modify the same checked-in contract without a dependency path or named merge owner.
findings.evidence: Both tasks write packages/contracts/order.ts and declare resources=[order-contract]. T2 and T4 both have after=[T1]. No merge owner exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Concurrent contract edits can conflict or overwrite one another, leaving producer and consumer changes based on different definitions.
findings.fix: Add T2 as a prerequisite of T4 so its contract patch follows generation, then verify both producer and consumer compile against the final checked-in definition.

findings.issue: The verification command short-circuits on failure and does not explicitly capture each check's exit status.
findings.evidence: command='npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit'; acceptance='record the exit status of all three checks, including if lint fails'.
findings.failure_scenario: If lint fails, typecheck and unit tests never execute; if typecheck fails, unit tests never execute. The required three exit statuses cannot be recorded.
findings.fix: Run all three checks independently, capture and record each exit status immediately, and report overall failure if any check fails.
